The Chiral Anomaly and the Wess-Zumino Term. A fundamental symmetry breaking occurs here. The causal structure of inference ( t → t + 1 t\to t+1 ) explicitly breaks Time-Reversal ( 𝒯 \mathcal{T} ) symmetry. In ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) dimensions, this renders the Dirac operator chiral, leading to a chiral anomaly in the functional determinant. This implies that gauge invariance is lost on the boundary Σ \Sigma . To restore gauge invariance, the effective action must include a topological Wess-Zumino (WZ) term [ 35 , 36 ] . Mathematically, this term cannot be written solely as an integral over the ( 1 + 1 ) (1+1) -dimensional inference path Σ \Sigma ; it requires extending the field configuration into a virtual ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) -dimensional bulk ℳ \mathcal{M} such that ∂ ℳ = Σ \partial\mathcal{M}=\Sigma .
